I think sea salt kale chips are the best way to go if you're looking for something that's lightly seasoned and still delicious.

The recipe I use involves cutting them into small bite size pieces, but not too small because they shrink in the oven anyway. Then tossing them in a bowl with a bit of olive oil so that they're evenly coated, some recipes will tell you to use a splash of vinegar but I personally choose to leave that out. It's up to you to try though. Remember to also preheat the oven at around 135 Celsius (275 Fahrenheit).

Then I add a pinch of salt. When I over seasoned, I pretty much just took the salt shaker and went at it thinking I didn't use that much, so a pinch is ideal.

Then to ensure an even absorption of the olive oil and possibly vinegar if you chose to use it, massage the leaves with your hands for about 1-2 minutes until they feel softer and have a darker appearance. Once you've done that, take some baking paper or foil and line up a tray and then scatter your kale leaves around it. Then pop them in the oven for around 15 minutes until they're crispy, if they're still a bit raw looking and tasting, then another minute or two should do it.

You can also do the same with spinach!

What I do with my Kale-

Wrap golden beats individually in tin-foil. Put one garlic clove in each package with a small amount of olive oil. Cook in a preheated oven at 425˚ for about 20 minutes, or until you can easily push a fork through them. Cut into quarters.

Thinly slice shallots (or yellow onion) and place them into a heated pan with whole garlic cloves (scored) and olive oil. Cook on low for a couple of minutes.

Mix golden beats and shallots together, then add diced kale. Cook until the kale is tender and bright green... salt to taste.

I love deep greens, but kale is the one thing that I can't seem to stomach. It's so incredibly bitter, so I imagine some way to spice it in a sautee or as a secondary ingredient to something really flavorful would be a good idea.

I find kale to be really good for stir fries if you want to give that a go, it becomes a lot less bitter then.

Try with some sliced mushrooms (personally I really love oyster mushrooms in stir fries, but plain old button mushrooms will do the trick too), two handfuls of fine chopped kale, a diced onion, a clove of minced garlic, shredded bok choy, snow peas, peeled and grated ginger, diced beef and julienned carrots -- heat vegetable oil (or sesame oil) in a pan on high heat and add in the vegetables, stir for around 10-12 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the meat has browned.

Remove your stir fry from the pan and put into a bowl and stir in some salt, pepper and plum sauce.

You might want to add noodles in your stir fry or try eating it with rice. The kale acts as a cabbage replacement, it tastes less bitter and provides a nice texture and crunch to the meal. Worth a try!
